newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian groups launch clean-up campaign.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian groups launch clean-up campaign.

text.p: Three Nigerian groups including the umbrella trade union body NLC on Thursday launched a project to improve sanitation in their African country in order to save lives, especially the lives of children.
Ene Baba Owoh, spokesman for the groups, told a news conference in Lagos that their project -- Clean-Up Nigeria -- was conceived out of concern for the Nigerian environment.

"Cleaning up Nigeria is a huge affair, but a sensible one which must be embarked upon," Owoh said, adding that "Available data has shown many children die yearly from diseases caused by poor sanitary conditions."

Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the National Union of Road Transport Workers that groups all commercial vehicle owners and drivers, and Clean-Up Nigeria, a non-governmental organisation, were the three groups involved in the project, he said.
It is common on Nigeria's crowded streets and other public places to see mounds of refuse because of poor sanitary habit of many of its 100 million people.
Local authorities in charge of sanitation also frequently fail to clear rubbish.
The military authorities in 1984 decreed the last Saturday of every month a mandatory clean-up day but the exercise has since lost its spark.
Owoh said their own project would emphasise waste education and provision of waste baskets to all commercial vehicles.
